questions.question: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs for oxygenation.

questions.question: What is the pacemaker of the heart?
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the natural pacemaker of the heart, generating impulses at 60-100 beats per minute.

questions.question: What is the function of the mitral valve?
options: Prevents backflow from left ventricle to left atrium
Prevents backflow from right ventricle to right atrium
Prevents backflow from aorta to left ventricle
questions.correct_answer: Prevents backflow from left ventricle to left atrium
questions.explanation: The mitral (bicuspid) valve prevents backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular contraction.

questions.question: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. There are four pulmonary veins.

questions.question: What is the normal average cardiac output at rest?
questions.explanation: Average cardiac output at rest is approximately 5 L/min (heart rate × stroke volume = 70 bpm × 70 mL = 4.9 L/min).

questions.question: Which component of the ECG represents ventricular depolarization?
questions.explanation: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization (contraction). The P wave represents atrial depolarization.

questions.question: What is the functional unit of the cardiovascular system?
questions.explanation: Capillaries are the functional units of the cardiovascular system where gas and nutrient exchange occurs between blood and tissues.

questions.question: Which is the largest artery in the body?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the largest artery in the body. It carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the systemic circulation.
